subject: Exec arrival playbook — Lynx Commerce VP & CIO demo
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@lynxcommerce.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@lynxcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Exec arrival playbook — Lynx Commerce VP & CIO demo

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for locking in Wednesday 11:00 PT for the live demo. A few quick asks so we can make the exec portion high-impact and avoid last-minute scoping changes: 

- Can you confirm which two executives will attend (VP/Head of Product + CIO or VP + CTO)? Names/titles help us tailor the talking points.
- Arrival plan: are they joining for the whole 45-minute session or doing the 20-minute exec walkthrough only? If the latter, do they plan to join at 11:00 or ~11:10?
- AV/logistics: will they be in a conference room with AV or dialing from remote? If on-site, any check-in or security desk we should coordinate with?

Internal note: Ben will own the 10-minute technical deep-dive, Marissa will lead the commercial opening, Soojin will coordinate run-of-show and backup coverage. If execs arrive late, our plan is to start with the first 10 minutes of the demo and circle back for the exec walkthrough when they join — Ben will be prepared to do the walk-through for the CIO.

I attached a draft agenda and an “arrival playbook” for guest arrivals. If you can confirm the execs and arrival constraints by end of day today, we’ll finalize the calendar invite and the one-pager for your procurement team.

Thanks —
Hannah
Sr. Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(attachment: lynx-exec-agenda.pdf)
From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@lynxcommerce.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@lynxcommerce.com>

Date: 2027-05-01T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec arrival playbook — Lynx Commerce VP & CIO demo

Hannah —

Thanks for the plan and the agenda; the deck looked good in the snapshot. Quick answers:

- Confirmed attendees: Nora Patel (VP Product) and Samir Joshi (CIO). Nora will join for the full 45m; Samir will likely be ~10 minutes late — he has back-to-back operational reviews that morning. Either way, Samir wants the short technical deep-dive.
- They will be remote — joining from our NY office conference room via Zoom. AV will be handled by our facilities team; I can provide the room dial-in if needed.
- Procurement: Priya is looped for contract/terms questions.

If you can lead with the customer-facing narrative and reserve the last 10 minutes for a technical Q&A, that should work. Appreciate Ben prepping the deeper demo for Samir.

Alex
Director of Product, Lynx Commerce

Hannah / team —

Thanks Alex for the quick confirmation — noted Nora (VP Product) full presence, Samir (CIO) ~+10. Draft internal run-of-show below (we can push times +/- 2 minutes as needed):

- 11:00–11:05: Welcome & outcomes (Marissa)
- 11:05–11:15: Customer narrative / high-level value props (Hannah)
- 11:15–11:30: Live demo: core flows (Marissa + Hannah)
- 11:30–11:40: Technical deep-dive (Ben) — reserve for Samir; if Samir not present start Q&A; Ben to drop into KV-cache slide + perf numbers.
- 11:40–11:45: Next steps & procurement checkpoint (Hannah / Priya)

Contingency / coverage
- If Samir drops in late, Ben pivots to the deep-dive immediately and we move Q&A after.
- If both execs arrive >15 mins late, we start with the core demo and offer a 15-minute follow-up 1:1 with Samir the following day.

Logistics: I’ll upload the final slides to the shared Drive folder and will include a short 1-page checklist for facilities (Zoom link, passcode, contact for room tech). Ben — can you confirm the 3 bullet tech points you want to highlight so I can add them to the slides?

Thanks —
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

All —

Quick confirmation: I’ll lead the technical deep-dive and highlight these three points:
1) Latency & steady-state throughput for their median prompt length (we’ll show a 95th percentile chart)
2) Prefix/KV-cache use case mapped to their multi-customer context (how caching reduces token costs)
3) Failure/fallback story — model fallbacks and routing policy example (short diagram).

I’ll prep two backup slides in case Samir wants a deeper ops conversation. Good to sync on Friday 10:30 PT for a 20-min dry run?

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
